idiom_name: duck-typed view object + plain presenter class (modules for shared behaviour)
implementation_notes: Ruby declares no interfaces: the presenter simply calls query/show_total on whatever view object it was given, the contract is documented (or enforced with respond_to? checks) rather than typed, and a test double is any object implementing the same methods. Duck typing and module mixins replace the classic view interface, and the presenter stays a plain class so tests need no GUI toolkit. Keep the classic delegation object when a screen must implement several contracts and explicit forwarding is clearer than dynamic dispatch. Where a Ruby GUI binding (GTK, Shoes, FXRuby) is used, its callbacks should only forward to the presenter; the presenter should not require the toolkit.
pitfalls: method_missing-based forwarding hides a missing view method until the user interacts; define methods explicitly or implement respond_to_missing? so failures surface in tests.
Blocks passed into widget APIs are closures capturing the presenter; clear callbacks when a widget is destroyed or the presenter and its model stay reachable.
GUI bindings are not thread-safe; a presenter driven from a background thread must hand updates back to the toolkit's main loop.
